messages.author: 0ee8ae7c0d185529
messages.subject: blavInspect issue
parts:
Greetings,

I am receiving this message

When I run this part of the a growth curve model

fitGenDiffNonLinBayes <- bgrowth(BayesnonLinGCM, data=newdataGenDiff1
              ,target="jags",save.lvs=TRUE,burnin=10000, sample=200000)

I receive two messages.

WARNING ** blavaan (0.3-4) did NOT converge after 1100 adapt+burnin iterations

I did run this code with 10000 adapt steps and received the same message.  I do get output that
seems sensible.  But, when I then run

lvmeans1 <- blavInspect(fitGenDiffNonLinBayes, "lvmeans")

I receive the following message.

Error in UseMethod("lavInspect", object) : 
  no applicable method for 'lavInspect' applied to an object of class "blavaan"

I know that this has been discussed about a year ago, but I am wondering if there is a resolution.

Thanks

David

messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: Re: blavInspect issue
parts:
David

I see you are running blavaan 0.3-4, I think this issue is fix in the development version (https://faculty.missouri.edu/~merklee/blavaan/source.html).

As I can run the following example with blavaan_0.3-5.403

library(blavaan)

## linear growth model with a time-varying covariate
model.syntax <- '
  # intercept and slope with fixed coefficients
    i =~ 1*t1 + 1*t2 + 1*t3 + 1*t4
    s =~ 0*t1 + 1*t2 + 2*t3 + 3*t4

  # regressions
    i ~ x1 + x2
    s ~ x1 + x2

  # time-varying covariates
    t1 ~ c1
    t2 ~ c2
    t3 ~ c3
    t4 ~ c4
'

fit <- bgrowth(model.syntax, data=Demo.growth, target="jags",save.lvs=TRUE)
summary(fit)

lvmeans1 <- blavInspect(fit, "lvmeans")
head(lvmeans1)

messages.author: 645e2b041ea2a63e
messages.subject: Re: blavInspect issue
parts:
Hi David,

For the reinstalling part, try a separate

install.packages("lavaan")

command before the command that installs blavaan. (You get that error
because R is trying to install lavaan from my server, but I only have
blavaan on my server.)

Hopefully that solves your problem. To make sure, you might do a test
run with, say, only 50 adapt/burnin/sampling iterations. Then you can
see whether it works without waiting for 200k samples.

Ed
